The company is known for its well-designed apparel, accessories, and home goods. Ugmonk…"; ChatGPT: "Ugmonk.com is not a website for a local business in the traditional sense. It is an online store that sells a variety of products, including…"; ChatGPT: "Ugmonk is a design-focused brand founded by Jeff Sheldon that offers a range of products including apparel, accessories, and home office goods. Known for its…". Saying clearly who you are and what you do in your llms.txt file, structured data and homepage gives AI assistants that read your site the right description. It does not change what a model has already learned, so results can take time to change. This row is for information and is not counted again in your score.

gaps.notes: no card at /.well-known/mcp.json or /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json; an MCP server was found (an MCP endpoint answered at https://ugmonk.com/api/mcp) but it is not advertised with a server card
gaps.remediation: We found no MCP discovery card at https://ugmonk.com/.well-known/mcp.json or https://ugmonk.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json. If you run an MCP server, publish a JSON card at one of those addresses with the server's name and a transports list giving its URL (server cards are still a draft proposal, so the format may change). If you don't run one, building an MCP server is a development project, worth it only if you have tools or data you want AI agents to use, such as booking, ordering or account lookups. Estimated effort: 30 minutes to 1 hour for the card; several days to build a new MCP server.

gaps.notes: 3% of scored test answers matched how your site describes itself and included at least one link to it.
gaps.remediation: You cannot edit ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity directly, so there is no setting that makes them link to your site. What can help is having pages worth citing: one clear page for each thing you offer, each at a single stable address with a canonical URL, that answers the question in plain text near the top. Links to those pages from independent sources, such as directories, press coverage and industry lists, can also help, because these models draw on what other sites say. Estimated effort: 2 to 4 hours.

We found no Service, Product or Offer structured data on your homepage (this check reads the homepage only). If you sell services, add a Service block for each main service with name, description and provider (your Organization); if you sell products, use Product with an Offer, adding a price only if you publish one. If your site doesn't sell anything, this check doesn't fit it and you can leave it. Estimated effort: 1 to 3 hours.

gaps.notes: no card or no tools declared
gaps.remediation: Depends on Well-known discovery: there is no discovery card to read tools from. If you publish a card, list each tool your MCP server offers in its tools array, with a name, a plain-language description and an inputSchema. Estimated effort: 30 minutes to 1 hour.

gaps.notes: 45% of scored test answers named your domain and matched how your site describes itself. Of the 40 scored answers, 30 matched how your site describes itself, 4 described a different person or business than your site says it is, 4 did not say enough to check, and 2 did not show that the model knew your site. 40 of 40 test answers could be scored, across 4 AI models. Average by model: ChatGPT 20, Claude 35, Gemini 40, Perplexity 27.
gaps.remediation: You cannot edit ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity directly, so there is no setting to change here. What can help these models name your business is clear content on your own site that says who you are, what you do and who you serve, using your business name and domain; Organization or LocalBusiness structured data on your homepage; the same business name, address and description everywhere you are listed; and mentions on independent sources these models read, such as directories, press coverage, industry lists and reviews on third-party platforms. Estimated effort: 4+ hours.

gaps.check_name: Models treat your domain as the principal answer
gaps.notes: 43% of scored test answers matched how your site describes itself and put your domain in the first half of the answer, rather than only mentioning it at the end.
gaps.remediation: You cannot edit ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity directly. What can help them present your business as a main answer rather than a passing mention is stating plainly, near the top of your homepage and key pages, who you are, what you do and who you serve, with your business name and domain; structured data (such as Organization or LocalBusiness) that says the same thing; and the same description of your business on the third-party sites that list you. Estimated effort: 2 to 4 hours.
